extracted.intended_audience: children's book writers / authors aiming for literary awards
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the American Library Association's criteria and eligibility for the John Newbery Medal — what kinds of children's books (genre, age range, publication timing) are considered and the literary qualities the committee evaluates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — American children's book; publication timeframe; genres; age range
rubrics_metrics.description: The Newbery Medal is awarded annually by the ALA for "the most distinguished American children's book published in the previous year." The 15-member committee accepts works of fiction, nonfiction, and poetry for children up to age 14, for a book published in the previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry must be an American children's book published in the prior year; acceptable forms include fiction, nonfiction, and poetry; intended readership should be children up to age 14. Each year the committee reads hundreds of books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of the theme or concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation of the theme or concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee evaluates how effectively the work develops and expresses its central theme or conceptual focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of information (accuracy, clarity, and organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of information including accuracy, clarity, and organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether information is factually accurate (for nonfiction), clearly expressed, and well organized for the intended child audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of a plot
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee looks at the strength and coherence of the narrative arc and how the plot unfolds for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delineation of characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators consider how clearly and convincingly characters are portrayed and developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delineation of a setting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The vividness, specificity, and appropriateness of the setting for the story and its effects on mood and understanding are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style should suit the book's content and intended child audience; varied forms (e.g., novel-in-verse such as The Crossover) may be recognized if the style is effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional impact — evokes strong emotions in the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Think about how your theme, characters, plot, and setting will evoke strong emotions in the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are advised to craft elements (theme, character, plot, setting) that produce strong emotional responses in children and adult gatekeepers (librarians, parents, critics), as emotional resonance contributes to a book being seen as 'distinguished.'
